name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: China's rare-earth export pause expires 10 Nov with no renewal; US tariffs ~7%
state: China's one-year suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov, and no renewal had been announced as of 2 Nov; its April 2025 licensing rules remain in force. Lapsed controls would reinstate tighter licensing. US Section 301 tariffs keep the average effective rate near 7%.
for_you: Tariffs and export controls can raise prices for electronics, cars and other goods with Chinese parts.
rubric_hit: Major export controls pending renewal; tariffs elevated = Watch

sources.title: Startup Fortune — China's rare earth export truce expires 10 November with no renewal in sight
FXStreet — China's rare earth leverage has an expiration date: 10 November

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
